{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_2f1fc4bdc7c44e96b152a836","type":"tool_result","content":"name: CI\n\non:\n  pull_request:\n  push:\n    branches: [main]\n  # Manual runs: re-checking a branch against a moved main, or confirming a gate after\n  # changing one, without pushing an empty commit.\n  workflow_dispatch:\n  # An advisory published after a merge is invisible until someone opens a pull request, and this\n  # repository can go days without one. Monday 07:00 UTC; only `build-chain` answers it.\n  schedule:\n    - cron: '0 7 * * 1'\n\n# Every job here only reads the checkout; the repo default is write.\npermissions:\n  contents: read\n\n# A newer push to the same branch supersedes an in-flight run. main is exempt:\n# every commit there should have its own recorded result.\nconcurrency:\n  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}\n  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}\n\njobs:\n  verify:\n    name: Verify\n    # The scheduled run exists for the dependency audit; re-running the suite on an unchanged\n    # tree every Monday would report nothing new.\n    if: github.event_name != 'schedule'\n    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1\n        with:\n          persist-credentials: false\n          # Full history, not for this job but for the spec anchor check below:\n          # it resolves cited content from\n          # origin/main, which a shallow clone cannot serve.\n          fetch-depth: 0\n\n      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0\n        with:\n          node-version: '22'\n          cache: npm\n\n      # --ignore-scripts so `prepare` does not build on install: what a lifecycle script\n      # runs is out of this workflow's control, and the Build step below is where a broken\n      # compile should be reported. Type check catches it earlier still.\n      - name: Install\n        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts\n\n      # Every `npm run` step below is one link of the `verify` script in\n      # package.json, in the same order - scripts/verify-script.test.ts holds\n      # the two together - and kept as separate steps so a red run names the\n      # gate that failed rather than a single opaque command.\n      - name: Type check\n        run: npm run typecheck\n\n      # example/ is outside tsconfig.json's rootDir, so nothing checked the one\n      # file the README and the guide are written against.\n      - name: Type check the example\n        run: npm run typecheck:example\n\n      - name: Lint (--max-warnings 0)\n        run: npm run eslint\n\n      # Reports, never blocks. The one rule it runs is `warn`, so the step exits\n      # 0 on its own and carries no continue-on-error: a non-zero exit here now\n      # means the config itself broke, and that should fail. Its findings render\n      # as warning annotations rather than failures, which is what a report on a\n      # passing check should look like.\n      #\n      # require-statement-links counts spec statements with no test behind them.\n      # Most of what it reports needs a test written rather than a line changed,\n      # so the count is meant to be visible on every run and to fall over time.\n      # Its test-side mirror, require-spec-link, is satisfied and gates in the\n      # Lint step above. Never add a rule here to escape a red gate -\n      # eslint.config.backlog.mjs says what belongs.\n      - name: Spec traceability backlog (report)\n        run: npm run lint:backlog\n\n      - name: Format check\n        run: npm run prettier:check\n\n      # Runs the whole suite and fails it on the committed coverage floor in\n      # jest.config.js, so this is the test gate rather than an extra pass.\n      - name: Test (with coverage floor)\n        run: npm run test:coverage\n\n      - name: Build\n        run: npm run build\n\n      # Anchors drift silently: a cited file gaining or losing lines above the\n      # cited one leaves the link pointing at different content, and the spec\n      # still reads as cited. Resolves content at origin/main, which the\n      # fetch-depth: 0 above exists to provide. A red check is fixed by running\n      # `node scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.mjs` and committing the result.\n      - name: Spec anchor check\n        run: node scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.mjs --check origin/main\n\n      # A citation counts as coverage only in its statement's trailing\n      # parenthetical; one written mid-statement is dropped by the Lore job in silence,\n      # so the spec reads as cited while its coverage is zero. A red check is\n      # fixed by moving the link to the end of its statement, never by deleting\n      # it (AGENTS.md § Spec Test Links).\n      # Every fenced typescript block in the three documented files is generated\n      # from source; hand transcription is what produced the defects this catches.\n      - name: Documented code blocks\n        run: npm run docs:check\n\n      # Three rules that held only because somebody remembered them: a path in prose that resolves,\n      # a spike that says it is a spike, and an example region inside the EU.\n      - name: Documented paths resolve\n        run: npm run docs:check-paths\n\n      - name: Spike documents carry a status block\n        run: npm run docs:check-spikes\n\n      - name: Documented regions\n        run: npm run check:regions\n\n      # A line number is a derived pointer; the name is what the author cited. This catches a citation\n      # whose line moved under it, which no baseline comparison can see on a branch that edits the spec.\n      - name: Spec citations name their test\n        run: npm run spec:names\n\n      - name: Spec link placement\n        run: npm run check:spec-links\n\n      # Lead paragraphs and a spec's status-vs-coverage are ESLint's job; the\n      # one verdict a `files` glob cannot express - that an ADR's frontmatter\n      # status parses, without holding the ADR to the coverage tier - is this\n      # script's. `check:spec-status -- --coverage` lists unlinked statements\n      # and never gates.\n      - name: Spec status\n        run: npm run check:spec-status\n\n      # A release note and a commit subject have different readers, so this is a\n      # file the author writes rather than something derived from the log. The\n      # label is the escape hatch for a src/ change nothing installable observes.\n      - name: Changelog entry\n        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && !contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'no-changelog')\n        # No fetch: the checkout above resolves every head into refs/remotes\n        # with fetch-depth 0, and its credential is gone by the time a step\n        # runs, so fetching here asked an unauthenticated git for a private\n        # repository and exited 128 before the gate was ever reached.\n        run: bash scripts/check-changelog.sh \"origin/${{ github.base_ref }}\"\n\n  # Separate job, not a step on `verify`: these two check what the build chain\n  # pulls in rather than what the code does, and a red audit should not read as\n  # a failing test suite. It needs the tree installed but nothing built, so it\n  # skips `prepare` with --ignore-scripts.\n  build-chain:\n    name: Build chain\n    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1\n        with:\n          persist-credentials: false\n\n      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0\n        with:\n          node-version: '22'\n          cache: npm\n\n      - name: Install (no build)\n        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts\n\n      # Full tree, dev included: those packages are what a runner installs\n      # before building dist/, and the release workflow signs what it produces.\n      - name: Audit (high and above)\n        run: npm run check:audit\n\n      # A tag is a mutable pointer its owner can repoint under a job that holds\n      # repository credentials.\n      - name: Action pins\n        run: npm run check:action-pins\n\n  # Its own job because it is the only check that exercises the package as a\n  # consumer receives it - packed, installed outside this tree, with no optional\n  # peer present. Everything else here tests the source in place, where every\n  # dependency is already installed and every one of these failures is invisible.\n  smoke:\n    name: Smoke (packed tarball)\n    if: github.event_name != 'schedule'\n    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1\n        with:\n          persist-credentials: false\n\n      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0\n        with:\n          node-version: '22'\n          cache: npm\n\n      - name: Install (no build)\n        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts\n\n      # Explicit, rather than relying on `npm pack` to trigger `prepare`: a build failure should be\n      # reported by a step named Build, not as a confusing pack error inside the smoke script.\n      - name: Build\n        run: npm run build\n\n      # Two variants, two jobs' worth of signal in one: `bare` is a mock-provider consumer with no\n      # optional peer, `full` is a Bedrock or Vertex consumer with both. They fail differently and\n      # separate steps name which consumer is broken.\n      - name: Smoke (no optional peer)\n        run: npm run smoke -- bare\n\n      - name: Smoke (both optional peers)\n        run: npm run smoke -- full\n--- helpers ---\nimport type {Message, MessageChunk, ToolCall, UsageMetadata} from '../types/ai.js';\nimport type {ToolRegistry} from './tools/registry.js';\n\nexport function shouldContinueToolLoop(\n  stopReason: string,\n  pendingToolCalls: ToolCall[],\n  toolRegistry: ToolRegistry | undefined\n): boolean {\n  return stopReason === 'tool_use' && pendingToolCalls.length > 0 && toolRegistry !== undefined;\n}\n\nexport async function collectText(stream: AsyncGenerator<MessageChunk>): Promise<string> {\n  let text = '';\n  for await (const chunk of stream) {\n    if (chunk.type === 'text') text += chunk.text;\n  }\n  return text;\n}\n\nexport function buildToolCallMessages(pendingToolCalls: ToolCall[]): Message {\n  return {\n    role: 'assistant',\n    content: pendingToolCalls.map(tc => ({\n      type: 'tool_use' as const,\n      toolUseId: tc.id,\n      name: tc.name,\n      input: tc.input,\n    })),\n  };\n}\n\nexport function collectToolCalls(chunk: MessageChunk, pendingToolCalls: ToolCall[]): void {\n  if (chunk.type === 'tool_use') pendingToolCalls.push(chunk.toolCall);\n}\n\nexport function extractStopReason(chunk: MessageChunk): string | null {\n  return chunk.type === 'stop' ? chunk.stopReason : null;\n}\n\nexport function extractUsage(chunk: MessageChunk): UsageMetadata | undefined {\n  return chunk.type === 'stop' ? chunk.usage : undefined;\n}\n--- index exports re usage/hooks ---\n15:  OrchestratorHooks,\n72:  UsageMetadata,\n83:} from './types/ai.js';\n84:export {AIError} from './types/ai.js';","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"e207b6aa-d852-44b2-b5e7-c28649cbdcfb","uuid":"8650d6d9-af2c-48d2-b179-c6857eb50a86","timestamp":"2026-11-01T18:26:26.391Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"name: CI\n\non:\n  pull_request:\n  push:\n    branches: [main]\n  # Manual runs: re-checking a branch against a moved main, or confirming a gate after\n  # changing one, without pushing an empty commit.\n  workflow_dispatch:\n  # An advisory published after a merge is invisible until someone opens a pull request, and this\n  # repository can go days without one. Monday 07:00 UTC; only `build-chain` answers it.\n  schedule:\n    - cron: '0 7 * * 1'\n\n# Every job here only reads the checkout; the repo default is write.\npermissions:\n  contents: read\n\n# A newer push to the same branch supersedes an in-flight run. main is exempt:\n# every commit there should have its own recorded result.\nconcurrency:\n  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}\n  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}\n\njobs:\n  verify:\n    name: Verify\n    # The scheduled run exists for the dependency audit; re-running the suite on an unchanged\n    # tree every Monday would report nothing new.\n    if: github.event_name != 'schedule'\n    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1\n        with:\n          persist-credentials: false\n          # Full history, not for this job but for the spec anchor check below:\n          # it resolves cited content from\n          # origin/main, which a shallow clone cannot serve.\n          fetch-depth: 0\n\n      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0\n        with:\n          node-version: '22'\n          cache: npm\n\n      # --ignore-scripts so `prepare` does not build on install: what a lifecycle script\n      # runs is out of this workflow's control, and the Build step below is where a broken\n      # compile should be reported. Type check catches it earlier still.\n      - name: Install\n        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts\n\n      # Every `npm run` step below is one link of the `verify` script in\n      # package.json, in the same order - scripts/verify-script.test.ts holds\n      # the two together - and kept as separate steps so a red run names the\n      # gate that failed rather than a single opaque command.\n      - name: Type check\n        run: npm run typecheck\n\n      # example/ is outside tsconfig.json's rootDir, so nothing checked the one\n      # file the README and the guide are written against.\n      - name: Type check the example\n        run: npm run typecheck:example\n\n      - name: Lint (--max-warnings 0)\n        run: npm run eslint\n\n      # Reports, never blocks. The one rule it runs is `warn`, so the step exits\n      # 0 on its own and carries no continue-on-error: a non-zero exit here now\n      # means the config itself broke, and that should fail. Its findings render\n      # as warning annotations rather than failures, which is what a report on a\n      # passing check should look like.\n      #\n      # require-statement-links counts spec statements with no test behind them.\n      # Most of what it reports needs a test written rather than a line changed,\n      # so the count is meant to be visible on every run and to fall over time.\n      # Its test-side mirror, require-spec-link, is satisfied and gates in the\n      # Lint step above. Never add a rule here to escape a red gate -\n      # eslint.config.backlog.mjs says what belongs.\n      - name: Spec traceability backlog (report)\n        run: npm run lint:backlog\n\n      - name: Format check\n        run: npm run prettier:check\n\n      # Runs the whole suite and fails it on the committed coverage floor in\n      # jest.config.js, so this is the test gate rather than an extra pass.\n      - name: Test (with coverage floor)\n        run: npm run test:coverage\n\n      - name: Build\n        run: npm run build\n\n      # Anchors drift silently: a cited file gaining or losing lines above the\n      # cited one leaves the link pointing at different content, and the spec\n      # still reads as cited. Resolves content at origin/main, which the\n      # fetch-depth: 0 above exists to provide. A red check is fixed by running\n      # `node scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.mjs` and committing the result.\n      - name: Spec anchor check\n        run: node scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.mjs --check origin/main\n\n      # A citation counts as coverage only in its statement's trailing\n      # parenthetical; one written mid-statement is dropped by the Lore job in silence,\n      # so the spec reads as cited while its coverage is zero. A red check is\n      # fixed by moving the link to the end of its statement, never by deleting\n      # it (AGENTS.md § Spec Test Links).\n      # Every fenced typescript block in the three documented files is generated\n      # from source; hand transcription is what produced the defects this catches.\n      - name: Documented code blocks\n        run: npm run docs:check\n\n      # Three rules that held only because somebody remembered them: a path in prose that resolves,\n      # a spike that says it is a spike, and an example region inside the EU.\n      - name: Documented paths resolve\n        run: npm run docs:check-paths\n\n      - name: Spike documents carry a status block\n        run: npm run docs:check-spikes\n\n      - name: Documented regions\n        run: npm run check:regions\n\n      # A line number is a derived pointer; the name is what the author cited. This catches a citation\n      # whose line moved under it, which no baseline comparison can see on a branch that edits the spec.\n      - name: Spec citations name their test\n        run: npm run spec:names\n\n      - name: Spec link placement\n        run: npm run check:spec-links\n\n      # Lead paragraphs and a spec's status-vs-coverage are ESLint's job; the\n      # one verdict a `files` glob cannot express - that an ADR's frontmatter\n      # status parses, without holding the ADR to the coverage tier - is this\n      # script's. `check:spec-status -- --coverage` lists unlinked statements\n      # and never gates.\n      - name: Spec status\n        run: npm run check:spec-status\n\n      # A release note and a commit subject have different readers, so this is a\n      # file the author writes rather than something derived from the log. The\n      # label is the escape hatch for a src/ change nothing installable observes.\n      - name: Changelog entry\n        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && !contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'no-changelog')\n        # No fetch: the checkout above resolves every head into refs/remotes\n        # with fetch-depth 0, and its credential is gone by the time a step\n        # runs, so fetching here asked an unauthenticated git for a private\n        # repository and exited 128 before the gate was ever reached.\n        run: bash scripts/check-changelog.sh \"origin/${{ github.base_ref }}\"\n\n  # Separate job, not a step on `verify`: these two check what the build chain\n  # pulls in rather than what the code does, and a red audit should not read as\n  # a failing test suite. It needs the tree installed but nothing built, so it\n  # skips `prepare` with --ignore-scripts.\n  build-chain:\n    name: Build chain\n    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1\n        with:\n          persist-credentials: false\n\n      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0\n        with:\n          node-version: '22'\n          cache: npm\n\n      - name: Install (no build)\n        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts\n\n      # Full tree, dev included: those packages are what a runner installs\n      # before building dist/, and the release workflow signs what it produces.\n      - name: Audit (high and above)\n        run: npm run check:audit\n\n      # A tag is a mutable pointer its owner can repoint under a job that holds\n      # repository credentials.\n      - name: Action pins\n        run: npm run check:action-pins\n\n  # Its own job because it is the only check that exercises the package as a\n  # consumer receives it - packed, installed outside this tree, with no optional\n  # peer present. Everything else here tests the source in place, where every\n  # dependency is already installed and every one of these failures is invisible.\n  smoke:\n    name: Smoke (packed tarball)\n    if: github.event_name != 'schedule'\n    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1\n        with:\n          persist-credentials: false\n\n      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0\n        with:\n          node-version: '22'\n          cache: npm\n\n      - name: Install (no build)\n        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts\n\n      # Explicit, rather than relying on `npm pack` to trigger `prepare`: a build failure should be\n      # reported by a step named Build, not as a confusing pack error inside the smoke script.\n      - name: Build\n        run: npm run build\n\n      # Two variants, two jobs' worth of signal in one: `bare` is a mock-provider consumer with no\n      # optional peer, `full` is a Bedrock or Vertex consumer with both. They fail differently and\n      # separate steps name which consumer is broken.\n      - name: Smoke (no optional peer)\n        run: npm run smoke -- bare\n\n      - name: Smoke (both optional peers)\n        run: npm run smoke -- full\n--- helpers ---\nimport type {Message, MessageChunk, ToolCall, UsageMetadata} from '../types/ai.js';\nimport type {ToolRegistry} from './tools/registry.js';\n\nexport function shouldContinueToolLoop(\n  stopReason: string,\n  pendingToolCalls: ToolCall[],\n  toolRegistry: ToolRegistry | undefined\n): boolean {\n  return stopReason === 'tool_use' && pendingToolCalls.length > 0 && toolRegistry !== undefined;\n}\n\nexport async function collectText(stream: AsyncGenerator<MessageChunk>): Promise<string> {\n  let text = '';\n  for await (const chunk of stream) {\n    if (chunk.type === 'text') text += chunk.text;\n  }\n  return text;\n}\n\nexport function buildToolCallMessages(pendingToolCalls: ToolCall[]): Message {\n  return {\n    role: 'assistant',\n    content: pendingToolCalls.map(tc => ({\n      type: 'tool_use' as const,\n      toolUseId: tc.id,\n      name: tc.name,\n      input: tc.input,\n    })),\n  };\n}\n\nexport function collectToolCalls(chunk: MessageChunk, pendingToolCalls: ToolCall[]): void {\n  if (chunk.type === 'tool_use') pendingToolCalls.push(chunk.toolCall);\n}\n\nexport function extractStopReason(chunk: MessageChunk): string | null {\n  return chunk.type === 'stop' ? chunk.stopReason : null;\n}\n\nexport function extractUsage(chunk: MessageChunk): UsageMetadata | undefined {\n  return chunk.type === 'stop' ? chunk.usage : undefined;\n}\n--- index exports re usage/hooks ---\n15:  OrchestratorHooks,\n72:  UsageMetadata,\n83:} from './types/ai.js';\n84:export {AIError} from './types/ai.js';","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"call_2f1fc4bdc7c44e96b152a836","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_97814e8893674bd59fd85e21","type":"tool_result","content":"#!/usr/bin/env node\n// Re-points specs' [validated by](../../src/X.test.ts#Lnn) anchors after\n// edits to the cited file - any cited\n// repository file, whatever its kind: each anchor's line number is\n// resolved to the content it cited in the base ref's copy of that file,\n// that content is found in the working copy (compared with quotes and\n// whitespace dropped, so a formatter pass is not drift), and the anchor is\n// rewritten to the match whose surrounding lines agree with the baseline's. When the cited\n// content occurs on several working lines, each candidate is scored by how\n// many of the baseline's neighbouring lines it reproduces at the same offsets;\n// a candidate whose context uniquely wins is chosen, and a tie is reported as\n// ambiguous for manual fix (exit 1 in both modes) instead of guessing. An\n// anchor into a file built of repeated blocks - a workflow whose jobs share an\n// identical setup - must therefore cite a line unique to its own step, because\n// the resolver refuses to guess between indistinguishable candidates.\n//\n// Usage:\n//   node scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.mjs [--check] [base-ref]\n//\n// base-ref defaults to origin/main and must be the baseline the anchors were\n// last correct against. Baseline line numbers are read from the base ref's\n// copy of each spec, never from the working copy, so re-running against the\n// same baseline is a no-op instead of a second translation. A spec whose\n// anchor set (the ordered list of test paths it cites) differs from the base\n// ref is skipped whole: its anchors were authored against the working tree,\n// and no baseline exists to repoint them from. An individual anchor whose\n// line number differs from the base spec's at the same position was\n// deliberately retargeted by a spec edit: it is accepted as authored, never\n// rewritten, and reported as \"retargeted (not checked)\".\n//\n// Independent of any baseline, every anchor must land on a line that exists\n// and carries content: an anchor whose target file is missing, whose line is\n// beyond the end of the file, or whose line is blank or closing punctuation\n// is reported as rotten and fails the run in both modes. An anchor\n// into a test file must additionally land on the it/test/describe declaration\n// itself, because a line inside a test body names no case a reader can check.\n// Non-test targets - a workflow, a config, package.json - are exempt from that\n// last check: they have no declaration to land on.\n//\n// Also independent of any baseline, a short-form [Lnnn](...#Lmmm) label must\n// name the line its own href points at. Labels are re-synced to their href\n// after the anchor rewrite, so a repointed href carries its label with it;\n// --check reports label/href disagreement as mislabelled and fails.\n// --check rewrites nothing, so it judges each label against its current\n// (un-repointed) href: a stale href is reported as stale, and once a plain run\n// repoints it the label follows, so the two runs still converge in one pass.\n//\n// --check rewrites nothing and exits 1 when any anchor is stale (its baseline\n// content now lives on a different line), unresolved (that content no\n// longer exists), rotten, or mislabelled. Without --check, stale anchors are\n// rewritten in place, labels are synced, and unresolved or rotten ones are\n// reported for manual fix with exit 1; a rotten anchor the rewrite itself\n// repoints needs no manual fix and is not reported.\n\nimport { execFileSync } from \"node:child_process\";\nimport { existsSync, readdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from \"node:fs\";\nimport { dirname, join, normalize } from \"node:path\";\nimport process from \"node:process\";\nimport { splitArgs } from \"./lib/cli-args.mjs\";\n\nconst TRACKED_PATH = String.raw`(?:\\.\\.\\/)+(?:scripts\\/[\\w./-]+|[\\w./-]+\\.[A-Za-z]+)`;\nconst ANCHOR = new RegExp(String.raw`(${TRACKED_PATH})#L(\\d+)`, \"g\");\n\n// A short-form [Lnnn](../../src/X.test.ts#Lmmm) link: its visible label is a\n// bare line number that must equal the href's #L number. The label has no\n// meaning apart from the href, so it is force-synced to the href even when the\n// href was manually retargeted; descriptive labels ([validated by], ...) never\n// match and are never touched.\nconst LABEL_LINK = new RegExp(String.raw`\\[L(\\d+)\\]\\((${TRACKED_PATH})#L(\\d+)\\)`, \"g\");\n\nconst { flags, positional } = splitArgs(process.argv.slice(2));\n\nif (flags.some((flag) => flag !== \"--check\") || positional.length > 1) {\n  process.stderr.write(\"usage: repoint-spec-anchors.mjs [--check] [base-ref]\\n\");\n  process.exit(2);\n}\nconst checkMode = flags.includes(\"--check\");\nconst baseRef = positional[0] ?? \"origin/main\";\n\nconst root = process.cwd();","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"e207b6aa-d852-44b2-b5e7-c28649cbdcfb","uuid":"64c86312-7362-4327-8cd5-a202c6a87ef1","timestamp":"2026-11-01T18:29:08.220Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"#!/usr/bin/env node\n// Re-points specs' [validated by](../../src/X.test.ts#Lnn) anchors after\n// edits to the cited file - any cited\n// repository file, whatever its kind: each anchor's line number is\n// resolved to the content it cited in the base ref's copy of that file,\n// that content is found in the working copy (compared with quotes and\n// whitespace dropped, so a formatter pass is not drift), and the anchor is\n// rewritten to the match whose surrounding lines agree with the baseline's. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_49a8def2338941bb99739358","type":"tool_result","content":"#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# Fails when a diff touches src/ and leaves CHANGELOG.md alone.\n#\n# Usage:\n#   bash scripts/check-changelog.sh [base-ref]     # default: origin/main\n#\n# The rule is about what a consumer can observe, not about effort: anything that\n# changes shipped behaviour needs a sentence they can read on npm. A change to\n# src/ that genuinely is not user-visible - an internal refactor, a test-only\n# edit - takes the `no-changelog` label instead, which is a deliberate, visible\n# act rather than a silent omission.\nset -uo pipefail\n\nbase=\"${1:-origin/main}\"\n\n# A base ref that does not resolve means nothing was compared. On a laptop that\n# is ordinary - a fresh clone has no origin/main - and skipping is right. In CI\n# it is the gate passing without running, which is the one outcome a gate must\n# never have, and it is exactly how a fetch that failed went unnoticed.\nif ! git rev-parse --verify --quiet \"$base\" >/dev/null; then\n  if [ -n \"${GITHUB_ACTIONS:-}\" ]; then\n    echo \"check-changelog: FAILED - base ref '$base' does not resolve, so nothing was checked\" >&2\n    exit 1\n  fi\n  echo \"check-changelog: base ref '$base' not found; skipping\" >&2\n  exit 0\nfi\n\nmerge_base=\"$(git merge-base \"$base\" HEAD)\"\nchanged=\"$(git diff --name-only \"$merge_base\"..HEAD)\"\n=== version ===\n#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# Fails when a release tag and the committed package.json version disagree.\n#\n# Usage:\n#   bash scripts/check-version.sh v0.2.0   # before pushing the tag\n#   bash scripts/check-version.sh          # in CI, reads GITHUB_REF_NAME\n#\n# A committed script rather than an inline workflow step: a tag that has already\n# fired a publish cannot be un-pushed, so the check has to be runnable before the\n# tag exists.\n#\n# It also holds CHANGELOG.md to the version being tagged. check-changelog.sh only\n# asks that the file was touched, so the release rename was ungated and the\n# version shipped under a heading that never named it.\nset -euo pipefail\n\nrepo=\"$(cd \"$(dirname \"${BASH_SOURCE[0]}\")/..\" && pwd)\"\ntag=\"${1:-${GITHUB_REF_NAME:-}}\"\nversion=\"$(node -p \"require('$repo/package.json').version\")\"\n\nif [ -z \"$tag\" ]; then\n  echo \"check-version: no tag given and GITHUB_REF_NAME is unset\" >&2\n  echo \"check-version: package.json is at $version, so the tag to push is v$version\" >&2\n  exit 2\nfi","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"e207b6aa-d852-44b2-b5e7-c28649cbdcfb","uuid":"fdd8ae1e-e41f-40dc-b5f9-2c7b4d90523e","timestamp":"2026-11-01T18:34:00.130Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# Fails when a diff touches src/ and leaves CHANGELOG.md alone.\n#\n# Usage:\n#   bash scripts/check-changelog.sh [base-ref]     # default: origin/main\n#\n# The rule is about what a consumer can observe, not about effort: anything that\n# changes shipped behaviour needs a sentence they can read on npm. A change to\n# src/ that genuinely is not user-visible - an internal refactor, a test-only\n# edit - takes the `no-changelog` label instead, which is a deliberate, visible\n# act rather than a silent omission.\nset -uo pipefail\n\nbase=\"${1:-origin/main}\"\n\n# A base ref that does not resolve means nothing was compared. On a laptop that\n# is ordinary - a fresh clone has no origin/main - and skipping is right. In CI\n# it is the gate passing without running, which is the one outcome a gate must\n# never have, and it is exactly how a fetch that failed went unnoticed.\nif ! git rev-parse --verify --quiet \"$base\" >/dev/null; then\n  if [ -n \"${GITHUB_ACTIONS:-}\" ]; then\n    echo \"check-changelog: FAILED - base ref '$base' does not resolve, so nothing was checked\" >&2\n    exit 1\n  fi\n  echo \"check-changelog: base ref '$base' not found; skipping\" >&2\n  exit 0\nfi\n\nmerge_base=\"$(git merge-base \"$base\" HEAD)\"\nchanged=\"$(git diff --name-only \"$merge_base\"..HEAD)\"\n=== version ===\n#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# Fails when a release tag and the committed package.json version disagree.\n#\n# Usage:\n#   bash scripts/check-version.sh v0.2.0   # before pushing the tag\n#   bash scripts/check-version.sh          # in CI, reads GITHUB_REF_NAME\n#\n# A committed script rather than an inline workflow step: a tag that has already\n# fired a publish cannot be un-pushed, so the check has to be runnable before the\n# tag exists.\n#\n# It also holds CHANGELOG.md to the version being tagged. check-changelog.sh only\n# asks that the file was touched, so the release rename was ungated and the\n# version shipped under a heading that never named it.\nset -euo pipefail\n\nrepo=\"$(cd \"$(dirname \"${BASH_SOURCE[0]}\")/..\" && pwd)\"\ntag=\"${1:-${GITHUB_REF_NAME:-}}\"\nversion=\"$(node -p \"require('$repo/package.json').version\")\"\n\nif [ -z \"$tag\" ]; then\n  echo \"check-version: no tag given and GITHUB_REF_NAME is unset\" >&2\n  echo \"check-version: package.json is at $version, so the tag to push is v$version\" >&2\n  exit 2\nfi","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"call_49a8def2338941bb99739358","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}
